checks: Normalization yields a≥1/d>t>0. The ratio hypothesis and q<1 imply a−t<a−b, hence b<t and 0<c<R. In particular the largest coefficient is unique and each cap denominator is positive.

For W<1 the slice map has Jacobian (1−W)^(d−1), separates the variables, and integrates to the Beta(1,d) density d(1−W)^(d−1). The projected variable is aW+(1−W)Z with 0≤Z≤b. For every fixed z₀ in this range the tail is one for w≤z₀, the dth power on (z₀,a), and zero in volume for w≥a, including the null endpoint W=1. The conditional-law formula covers deterministic Z as well.

At each positive-radius reflected pair ±k, reversing the sign of β exchanges the two thresholds v±s. For v≥a the zero-shift cap has zero mass. For t≤v<a the denominator a−z₀≥a−b and numerator a−v≤a−t imply G(v)≤1/2. When v−s≥z₀ all three values agree with a convex positive-part power, and when v−s<z₀ the lower threshold alone contributes one. At v−s=z₀ the power is one, and at v+s=a it is zero. If both thresholds are in the full/null regimes their sum is exactly one, including threshold equalities.

At the fiber level, |β|k≥max{Rt,ar−Rt} implies one threshold is at most zero and the other is at least ar. The first cap is full by u≥0 and the second is null in d-volume, with the highest vertex included when the threshold equals ar. Each pair reaches its zero-shift bound at the same β=0. The base-zero fiber is independent of β and zero-radius fibers are volume-null. The own fiber and the N pairs exhaust the prescribed lattice fibers, also when N=0.

At zero tilt the other vertex heights are at most rb<Rt, including the vertex at zero. The three cases ar<Rt, ar=Rt and ar>Rt give, respectively, an empty cap, one volume-null vertex, and an edge-scaled simplex. Multiplying the d edge fractions by Vr^d yields V(ar−Rt)₊^d/[a∏(a−uⱼ)]=VCᵤ(r−c)₊^d. All factors are in (0,a], so Cᵤ≥1 with equality exactly for a coordinate normal. All positive-radius boundary traces are volume-null for nonzero u.

readability: The clipping discussion uses “null cap” in the volume sense and explicitly includes a closed cap meeting just the highest vertex. The formula is a minimum for one fixed continuous orientation.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The exact through-centroid cap minimum follows for every shared tilt and every radius in the complete symmetric census. The proof uses reflection and peak dominance, without needing discrete concavity.
